mcq.q: Which is an example of discriminative (predictive) AI?
o: Generating an image from a prompt
mcq.e: It tells things apart (spam or not).

mcq.q: Which is an example of generative AI?
mcq.e: It creates new content.

mcq.q: The three core discriminative tasks are:
mcq.e: Category, number, and value from time-ordered data.

mcq.q: Generative ML in your course is described as:
o: Predicting an outcome from given information
Generating new content or sequences from learned patterns, e.g. next-word prediction
mcq.e: Predictive ML predicts outcomes; generative ML generates content.

mcq.q: Supervised / unsupervised describes ____ while predictive / generative describes ____.
o: what it produces; how it learns
how it learns; what it produces
mcq.e: They overlap but are different dimensions.

mcq.q: According to the lecturer, generative ML equals:
o: Unsupervised ML + supervised fine-tuning + reinforcement learning
mcq.e: Three ingredients of training.

mcq.q: On the AI map, transformers sit inside:
o: Deep neural networks (within neural networks, within ML, within AI)
mcq.e: Nested circles: AI > ML > NN > DNN > transformers.

mcq.q: A transformer is best described as a deep learning model that:
o: Reads one word at a time only
Reads all the words together and decides which words matter to each other
mcq.e: The peer-notes one-sentence definition.

mcq.q: ChatGPT writes text by:
o: Predicting the next word again and again
mcq.e: One word at a time.

mcq.q: ChatGPT is an example of:
mcq.e: Software only, unlike self-driving cars.

mcq.q: Why is an RNN limited for long texts?
o: It works one step at a time and gradients vanish or explode over long chains
mcq.e: w^n repeated multiplication.

mcq.q: How does a transformer avoid the chain problem?
o: Each word looks directly at every other word (attention)
mcq.e: Long-range links need not travel along a chain.

mcq.q: (Background) A token is:
o: A piece of text (a word or part of a word) the model works with
mcq.e: E.g. 'unhappy' = 'un' + 'happy'.

mcq.q: (Background) An embedding is:
o: A list of numbers (vector) representing a token
mcq.e: Similar meanings get similar vectors; learned in training.

mcq.q: (Background) Why add positional information?
o: All words are read together, so word order must be supplied
mcq.e: 'dog bites man' differs from 'man bites dog'.

mcq.q: (Background) In attention, scores are turned into weights using:
o: Softmax, so the weights add to 1
mcq.e: Then a weighted sum of values.

mcq.q: (Background) Token C = (1,1) attends to A = (1,0), B = (0,1), C with weights 0.248, 0.248, 0.503. New C is about:
(Background) Multi-head attention means:
o: Several attentions run in parallel, each focusing on different relationships
mcq.e: Results are joined.

mcq.q: (Background) What follows self-attention inside a transformer block?
o: A feed-forward network (with add and normalise shortcuts)
mcq.e: Then blocks are stacked many times.

mcq.q: (Background) The last layer of a language model turns scores into next-token probabilities with:
mcq.e: Then picks or samples the next token.

mcq.q: (Background) Why can an LLM hallucinate?
o: It predicts a likely next token and may state false things confidently
mcq.e: RAG supplies facts to reduce guessing.

mcq.q: Your EU AI Act notes call very flexible models such as large language models:
mcq.e: General-purpose AI.

mcq.q: In the three-stage recipe, the unsupervised stage is:
o: Learning patterns from lots of unlabelled data
mcq.e: For text, the next word is its own label.

mcq.q: Supervised fine-tuning uses:
o: Examples of good question and answer pairs
mcq.e: Teaches instruction following.

mcq.q: The reinforcement stage improves the model with:
o: Rewards and penalties on its responses
mcq.e: The agent adjusts to collect more reward.

mcq.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
mcq.e: Discriminative = examiner; generative = artist.

mcq.q: The weights of a generative model are learned using:
o: The same forward pass, loss, backpropagation and gradient descent as other networks
mcq.e: Lesson 6 machinery.

mcq.q: Transformers can have billions of weights, which makes them:
o: Very hard to explain (a black box)
mcq.e: Link to explainable AI (Lesson 14).

written.q: Compare discriminative and generative AI with examples, and state the lecturer's caution about supervised, unsupervised, predictive and generative.
written.a: Discriminative (predictive) AI classifies or predicts from input: spam detection, face recognition, house price (classification, regression, forecasting). Generative AI creates new text, images, audio, video or code: ChatGPT, music generation. Examiner vs artist. Caution: supervised / unsupervised describe how a machine learns; predictive / generative describe what it produces; they overlap but are not the same.

written.q: Explain how a generative language model produces text, and where transformers sit on the AI map.
written.a: It predicts the next word from everything written so far, appends it, and repeats ('ChatGPT writes text one word at a time'). Transformers sit inside deep neural networks, which sit inside neural networks, inside machine learning, inside AI; a transformer reads all the words together and decides which words matter to each other. It is the architecture behind LLMs such as ChatGPT.

written.q: Why were RNNs and LSTMs not enough for long text, and how does attention help?
written.a: An RNN reads one step at a time along a chain; repeated multiplication by the loop weight (wn) makes gradients vanish or explode, so it forgets distant words (France → French). An LSTM gates a long-term lane but is still sequential. Self-attention lets every word look directly at every other word in one step (and in parallel), so long-range links need not travel along a chain. (Background material.)

written.q: (Background) Explain self-attention and compute the new representation for C = (1,1) attending to A = (1,0), B = (0,1) and itself (Q = K = V).
written.a: Each token compares itself with all tokens: scores = dot products divided by √d; softmax turns them into weights adding to 1; output = weighted sum of values. For C: scores (1, 1, 2)/√2 = 0.707, 0.707, 1.414; softmax weights 0.248, 0.248, 0.503; new C = 0.248(1,0) + 0.248(0,1) + 0.503(1,1) = (0.752, 0.752).

written.q: Describe the three-stage way a generative model is trained.
written.a: Generative ML = unsupervised ML + supervised fine-tuning + reinforcement learning. First learn the patterns of language or images from huge amounts of unlabelled data (for text the next word is its own label). Then fine-tune with labelled examples of good answers (supervised). Then improve with feedback: responses are rewarded or penalised (reinforcement learning). Weights are learned by forward pass, loss, backpropagation and gradient descent.

written.q: (Background) Why can an LLM hallucinate and how do prompt / context techniques reduce it?
written.a: It only predicts a likely next token, so it can state false things confidently. Context engineering or RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) places the exact facts in the prompt so the model does not have to guess (Lessons 1 and 2); clear prompts, examples and constraints also steer the output.
